thread:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert — elevated 5xx rate on canary 'canary-17' (redwood-gen-2) in us-west-2. Severity P2.

maria: I'm on it, pulling logs. seeing transformer pool OOMs and 502s from edge LB.

kevin: Deploy bot shows canary traffic at 5% and error rate jumped ~17:05 UTC. Short link: https://console.internal/ci/canary-17 

deploy-bot: Canary metrics snapshot:
```
canary_id: canary-17
traffic: 5%
5xx_rate: 12.1% (baseline 0.2%)
p95_latency: 1.1s
p99_latency: 2.3s
instances_healthy: 87%
```

sam: Recommendation: stop the rollout and siphon traffic off canary. If flag exists, flip it; otherwise do manual rollback.

maria: Can we try feature flag first? It's less disruptive. Flag is `feature.canary_2026_rollout`. @kevin can you flip?

kevin: Running propagation command now:
```
redwoodctl feature-flag set feature.canary_2026_rollout false --env=prod --region=us-west-2
```

kevin: Flag updated. Gateway caches may take ~30s to a couple mins. Initiating gradual traffic siphon: 5% -> 0% over 3m as a safe unwind.

maria: Observing traffic shift. 3rd-party tracer shows requests rerouting to stable. Error rate falling (now 4.5%). :thumbsup:

sam: Leaving some canary instances up for diagnostics. If errors pop back when we fully drain, we'll do a full rollback.

maria: Quick sanity smoke: ran curl to /health on a few nodes, some return 200 but a subset 502. Attaching sample log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T17:06:12Z service=transformer level=error msg="OOM allocating kv cache" node=i-0abcd
2026-03-15T17:06:13Z service=api level=error msg="upstream returned 502" request_id=xyz
```

kevin: Noted. KVM pressure on the canary pool. I kicked off a safe rollback command as backup (no traffic change yet):
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --deployment canary-17 --to stable-2026-03-10 --region=us-west-2 --no-confirm
```

deploy-bot: Rollback prepared (dry-run) — will execute if flag flip doesn't recover fully in 5 minutes.

maria: Current numbers: canary 5xx 3.2% (down from 12), overall customer-facing error bump limited to 0.6% of requests in us-west-2. No customer data loss reported. Logging ticket for postmortem.

eve: FYI raised a quick customer-impact note for SRE-runbook: "minor error spike for small subset of users in us-west-2, mitigation in progress". Pinged support to monitor escalations.

kevin: Can confirm flag flip completed and traffic drained to 0% for canary within 3m. Running smoke validation suite against stable:
```
redwoodctl test smoke --suite=canary-smoke --region=us-west-2
```

maria: Smoke tests passed (all critical paths green). p99 latency back to baseline. Rolling state: canary fully drained, rollback not executed.

sam: Good. We'll keep the canary instances isolated for logs and heap dumps. Please collect heapdumps from transformer nodes with OOMs: `gcore` + upload to /artifacts/canary-17/ for research.

kevin: Collected three heap dumps and attached to ticket #INC-4829.

maria: Triage decisions: 1) Abort rollout completely for this model variant, 2) keep rollout paused until root cause identified, 3) open postmortem and model-team follow-up.

eve: Assigning oncall follow-up to @eve for overnight watch and next-morning handoff to model team. Adding runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/canary-unwind

maria: Handoff: monitoring until 06:00 UTC. If errors resurface, escalate to P1 and execute full rollback command that kevin prepared. Otherwise, we'll reconvene in async postmortem channel in 4 hours.

kevin: One action item for tomorrow: add memory-killguard and lower max-batch-size for canary variant. I'll open a PR.

maria: Thanks all. Closing incident channel when overnight watch confirmed stable. :pray:
